name: Patscherkofel
kurzbeschreibung: The Patscherkofel is Innsbruck’s beloved local mountain, the 1964/76 Olympic venue, offering breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails.
preis: Bergbahn Berg- und Talfahrt ca. 27 € (Zirbenweg-Rundfahrt-Ticket ca. 32 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Patscherkofel (2,248 m) rises as an unmistakable rounded mountain peak south of Innsbruck, towering over the sunny subalpine plateaus of Igls and Patsch. Topped by its iconic red telecommunications spire, it is the cherished local mountain of Innsbruck residents and an internationally famed sports landmark: host to the Olympic downhill races during both the 1964 and 1976 Winter Games, the latter crowned by Austrian ski legend Franz Klammer's heart-stopping gold medal run. Today, the mountain serves as an all-season haven for hikers, families, and nature enthusiasts. Its northern slopes harbor one of the oldest, largest, and best-preserved continuous stone pine (Zirbe) forests in the European Alps, home to trees dating back more than 700 years. Adjacent to the upper cable car station, the University of Innsbruck maintains the highest-altitude botanical alpine garden in Austria.

Route & Requirements

The signature hiking attraction is the world-renowned Zirbenweg (Stone Pine Trail): departing the top station of the modern 10-seater Patscherkofelbahn (1,965 m), this gently undulating panoramic trail meanders for roughly 7 kilometers through ancient pine woodlands and wild alpine rose meadows to the Tulfeinalm beneath Mount Glungezer (walking time 2.5 hours, easy grade T1/T2, perfect for families and seniors). Summiteers can ascend from the lift station directly to the Patscherkofel summit cross: walking either the winding gravel mountain road or the steeper singletrack beside the Alpine Garden, hikers gain 280 vertical meters in about 60 minutes. The summit cross delivers an awe-inspiring 360-degree panorama sweeping over Innsbruck, the Nordkette ramparts, the Wipptal corridor to the Brenner Pass, and the Stubai glacier valleys. Sturdy walking shoes, sunglasses, and wind shells are recommended. Dogs on leashes are permitted on all trails and aboard the cable cars.

Visit & Arrival

Public transit provides effortless access: IVB regional city bus line "J" departs Innsbruck central train station every 10 to 15 minutes, whisking passengers straight to the valley terminal of Patscherkofelbahn in Igls (Römerstraße). Drivers take the Brenner motorway A13 (exit Innsbruck-Süd) or the local road up to Igls. Expansive parking facilities are located right at the base terminal.

Tips

Purchase the convenient "Zirbenweg Circular Ticket": it includes the Patscherkofel cable car ascent, the 7-km scenic trek along the Zirbenweg to Tulfeinalm, the Glungezerbahn chairlift descent to Tulfes, and the connecting shuttle bus back to your starting point. Enjoy lunch on the panoramic sun terrace at "Das Kofel" mountain restaurant, or stop at rustic Boscheben hut for artisanal cheeses and fresh alpine buttermilk.
